title: Halve head dim: 4 heads -> 8 heads (HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64)
description: HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64, so n_head/n_kv_head goes 4 -> 8 at unchanged model_dim 512; nothing else touched.
reflection: NEGATIVE, and cleanly so: val_bpb 1.000110 vs baseline 0.997358, i.e. 0.0028 worse. The comparison is as controlled as it gets here -- 50.3M params both ways, identical estimated FLOPs/token, 414.1M tokens vs ~412M, steady-state MFU 33.24% vs ~33%, peak VRAM 22.7GB vs 22.2GB. So the loss is pure model quality, not a throughput artifact: at dim 512 the model genuinely prefers 4 wide (128-dim) heads over 8 narrow (64-dim) ones. My prior that head count binds more than head width was wrong at this scale. Likely cause is that QK-norm plus 32 rotary frequency channels leaves a 64-dim head with too little room to represent distinct match patterns, while attention here is only ~20% of FLOPs so wide heads are cheap. Practical consequence for the group: head_dim 64 is ruled out; the open question left on this axis is the other direction (HEAD_DIM 256 = 2 heads), which I would rate as low-probability but is now the only untested point. I would not spend a slot on it before the shape axis (DEPTH / ASPECT_RATIO) and the fp32-logits throughput problem, both still untouched.
